scenes.caption:
A decision form can strand someone on a missing route.
PathProof checks a finite model and shows the exact failure.

This equipment-loan model has three fixed true/false inputs.
That creates eight combinations to check.

The input is plain JSON: named inputs, nodes and conditions.
No scripts or arbitrary expressions execute.

Validate the model, then run all eight combinations.
Six terminate; two are missing a next route.

Two finding groups summarize the problem:
a missing route and a training node no run visits.

Here is a counterexample: member=true, training=false.
The run stops at “Training complete?” with no matching edge.

Replay the path one step at a time. The fixed inputs
explain why this member cannot reach a terminal.

Inspect the actual conditions. The model has a route
for trained members, but none for training=false.

The example repair adds training=false → Book training.
This is a real model edit, so the old results are cleared.

Run every scenario again. All eight now terminate,
and every modeled node is visited.

The findings panel is clear. This conclusion covers
only this finite model and its fixed boolean inputs.

Inspect scenario 2 again: the untrained member now
reaches Book training instead of stopping at the question.

Export the audit and the model. The Markdown audit
includes findings, traces and the complete JSON model.

A second built-in example has a referral cycle.
Load it and run the same exhaustive check.

The replay repeats a node under the same fixed inputs.
That is evidence of a cycle inside this model.

Return to the complete borrowing flow and rerun it.
The saved export preserves the repair and its evidence.

Model → check → trace → repair → rerun. This does not
test a live form, timing, services or unmodeled behavior.
